blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — post-fall reassessment and individualized secondary prevention
stem: A hospitalized client falls despite an existing prevention plan. After the nurse assesses the client and addresses immediate injury concerns, which safety action best supports preventing a recurrence?

options.A: Continue the existing prevention plan unchanged and reinforce compliance, because a completed fall-risk assessment remains sufficient after the event.
options.B: Replace the individualized plan with the same standard fall bundle used for all clients so post-fall care is consistent across the unit.
options.C: Document the incident and continue routine monitoring, revising the prevention plan only if the fall caused a clinically important injury.
options.D: Conduct a post-fall review with the care team, identify contributing factors, and revise the individualized prevention plan based on the findings.

rationale: AHRQ PSNet describes fall prevention as individualized and multidisciplinary and specifically identifies a post-fall review as an opportunity for secondary prevention. After immediate injury assessment, the team should evaluate contributing factors and update the individualized prevention approach. D is therefore correct. A fails to reassess after a fall. B incorrectly substitutes a one-size-fits-all plan for individualized prevention. C treats documentation as sufficient and delays prevention-plan revision until injury occurs, whereas the post-fall event itself is an opportunity for secondary prevention.
educational_objective: After an inpatient fall, use a multidisciplinary post-fall review to identify contributing factors and update the individualized prevention plan to reduce recurrence risk.
source_organization: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ) — PSNet
source_version_date: UC Davis PSNet Editorial Team update June 15, 2024; last reviewed 2024; live page retrieved 2026-08-26
source_locator: Preventing Falls in Healthcare Settings: fall-prevention measures must be individualized; multidisciplinary responsibility; individualized plan responsive to risk factors, needs and preferences; postfall review as an opportunity to plan secondary prevention.
source_claim_supported: A post-fall team review should be used for secondary prevention and individualized fall-prevention planning should respond to patient-specific contributing factors.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential: perform focused assessments; recognize changes in condition; use precautions to prevent injury and complications associated with a diagnosis or procedure.
correction_summary: Rebuilt all options to remove distractor-only absolute wording and the correct-answer length cue while preserving the post-fall secondary-prevention construct.

audit_findings.stem: PASS — immediate injury assessment is explicitly completed, leaving recurrence prevention as the tested action.
audit_findings.option_A: PASS as distractor — plausible but fails to reassess contributing factors after a new event.
audit_findings.option_B: PASS as distractor — standardized elements may be useful, but AHRQ explicitly rejects one-size-fits-all prevention in favor of individualized plans.
audit_findings.option_C: PASS as distractor — documentation is necessary but does not substitute for post-fall secondary prevention and plan revision.
audit_findings.option_D: PASS — directly matches AHRQ individualized, multidisciplinary post-fall review guidance.
audit_findings.ambiguity: PASS — D uniquely addresses both post-fall review and individualized prevention-plan revision.
audit_findings.second_answer: EXCLUDED — A, B, and C omit or contradict the individualized post-fall reassessment required for secondary prevention.
audit_findings.cueing: PASS — options are parallel and balanced; no unique length or absolute-word cue remains.
audit_findings.blueprint: PASS — focused reassessment and prevention of recurrent injury align with Reduction of Risk Potential.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — challenged whether a standard bundle could be acceptable. AHRQ supports combinations of strategies but specifically states that prevention must be individualized and names post-fall review as secondary prevention; D remains uniquely best.
